Hi Anita — great to meet on the call last week. To put together an initial Dedicated proposal and fleet sketch (GPU mix, reserve vs burst, and a suggested canary plan), we need a short intake with a few workload specifics. If you can paste answers below or drop the telemetry CSV you mentioned, we’ll return a first-pass SKU map and cost bands within 2 business days.

Immediate questions:
- Primary traffic pattern: predictable steady-state, daily peak window, or highly bursty/spiky? Please indicate local times for peaks.
- Concurrent sessions vs concurrent requests: do you hold long-lived chat sessions (stateful) with KV cache reuse, or do most calls end in <2s?
- Token mix: average prompt tokens, average response tokens, and 95th/99th percentile response length (tokens).
- P99 latency SLO for interactive flows (ms) and acceptable fallback latency if remote model is used for degraded capacity.
- Tolerance to model-tier fallbacks: is quality > latency (i.e., prefer higher-quality model with >150ms baseline) or strict latency-first?
- Percent of requests that use retrieval/LLM+RAG (i.e., include a vector lookup) vs simple completions.
- Expected committed vCPU/GPU start date and length of term you’re comfortable committing to (monthly, 12mo, 24mo).
- Any hard compliance constraints (no shared tenancy, VPC-only, specific KMS) we should include in the design.

Attachments you referred to (telemetry export + SLO matrix) will accelerate the sizing. Proposed next step: 30m call Wed or Thu to walk the telemetry together. My calendar: https://cal.redwood.com/vanessa/30

Thanks —

Hi Vanessa — thanks, attaching the sample telemetry (telemetry CSV) and our internal SLO sheet. Answers inline below.

- Traffic pattern: daily steady with two pronounced peaks. Primary peak 09:00–11:00 PT, secondary 18:00–20:00 PT. Outside peaks we still have ~40% of peak qps. Expected monthly growth ~8% MoM initially.
- Sessions: stateful chat. ~60% of traffic reuses KV cache across the session (average session length 12 minutes). Rest are quick stateless completions.
- Token mix: avg prompt 45 tokens, avg response 120 tokens. 95th response ~450 tokens, 99th ~900 tokens (rare).
- Latency SLO: interactive flows p95 < 300ms, p99 < 600ms. Fallback tolerance: we prefer quality but cannot exceed p99 900ms.
- Fallback policy: soft fallback to a compact variant (quantized) acceptable for non-sensitive flows; sensitive queries must remain on the higher-quality variant.
- RAG usage: ~35% of requests call the retrieval pipeline before generation.
- Commit: target pilot commit Q1 2027; initial reserved capacity target 8 GPUs with burst pool for peak. Term: evaluating 12–24mo.
- Compliance: VPC-only, customer-managed KMS, SOC2 required.

We shared the telemetry export with your team drive link and ProcureOps is on copy for contract steps.

Best,
Anita Shah

Thanks for the forward — reviewed telemetry and sketched an initial fleet outline. High-level recommendations below (sketch attached to HubSpot deal and Drive).

- GPU mix: 6x A800 for steady-state (good memory for KV + long responses) + 4x A100s in burst pool for p95/p99 headroom on long responses. If Skylift prefers fewer SKUs, 8x A800 with autoscale policy + transient A100 spot replacements is acceptable.
- Throughput assumptions (conservative): A800 ~ 120 sustained qps for avg 120-token responses with 60% cache reuse; A100 burst ~ 220 qps for short responses but with much better headroom for 900-token tails.
- KV/cache: recommend reserving 16–24GB of host+GPU-side cache footprint per 1k concurrent sessions. Given session lengths (avg 12m) and 60% reuse, plan for ~48GB aggregate GPU cache across the reserved pool for steady state.
- Fallbacks/canary: primary model = high-quality fp16 variant, fallback = 4-bit quantized variant for non-sensitive traffic. Canary plan: start 5% traffic on burst A100s with fallback mapping for RAG flows, observe output quality and p99 over 72h, then widen to 25% before full split.
- Autoscale knobs: increase token-batching window slightly for peak windows (09:00–11:00 PT) and enable conservative queue-work stealing to reduce p99 spikes for long responses. Also suggest rate-limiting for very long tail requests (>= 900 tokens) with a retry/backoff ladder so fallback doesn't create cascading load.
- Cost band: estimated reserved + burst blended cost range $XXk–$YYk/month for pilot (range depends on committed term; 12mo lowers monthly effective price). Exact numbers in the attached sketch.

Next steps: I’ll drop the one-pager to Drive and link in HubSpot. Karthik — can you validate the cache sizing assumptions and add any constraints for VPC-enforced deployments (network egress patterns, NAT sizing)?
